details.overview: HRPF uses lawful information requests and public-interest research to raise concerns about public safety and institutional accountability in Mandi Bahauddin. details.approach: HRPF seeks public information through the Punjab Right to Information framework, follows up with the responsible public information officers and the Punjab Information Commission, and uses available records to prepare public-interest analysis and recommendations.

details.overview: HRPF followed up sewage-scheme repairs, drainage maintenance and departmental responsibility in Mianwal Ranjha. Its public updates describe attention to manhole levels and local drainage, while correspondence records the request for repair and lawful handover of the sewage scheme. A separate update reports Pandowal drain-cleaning work after representations to the responsible department.
details.challenge:
Damaged sewerage pipes and the condition of roadside openings required attention to support public health and sanitation. The report identifies repair and cleaning of the existing scheme as the immediate work undertaken.

A request for greater drainage capacity was also submitted. The report does not provide technical measurements or confirm that the capacity expansion was completed.
details.approach:
The reported intervention focused on cleaning the existing scheme, repairing broken pipes and raising the level of roadside openings. A separate institutional request addressed the capacity of the Fifth Drain.

The completed repairs and the pending capacity request are presented separately so visitors can understand the reported outcome accurately.

details.targetCommunity: Women residing at Dar-ul-Aman in Mandi Bahauddin
details.overview: HRPF pursued concerns about basic facilities, food, healthcare and cleanliness at Dar-ul-Aman in Mandi Bahauddin through the Provincial Ombudsman Punjab. The supplied decision records the department’s response about facility arrangements and the complainant’s satisfaction during review. HRPF’s public report also describes improvements in sanitation and facility management.
details.challenge:
The report describes poor sanitation and cleanliness, inadequate healthcare arrangements, weak oversight and deficiencies in monitoring. These conditions affected women living in a government shelter established to provide protection and rehabilitation.

The issue required an institutional response to the facilities and accountability concerns identified in the complaint.
details.approach:
HRPF brought the reported deficiencies to the attention of an oversight institution through a detailed complaint. The complaint called for urgent inspection, immediate rectification of deficiencies, administrative accountability and protection of residents’ rights.

Engagement with the Provincial Ombudsman’s office helped draw official attention to the shelter and initiate administrative inquiries and corrective measures.

outcomes: The concerns received official attention.
Administrative inquiries were initiated.
Corrective measures were undertaken.
The report records noticeable improvements in sanitation and facility management.
